newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wool prices mixed to lower at sales.
newsitem.headline: NZ wool prices mixed to lower at sales.

text.p: Wool prices were mixed to slightly easier at sales at Napier and Christchurch on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
The fine segment indicator rose six cents to $7.68, medium fell two to $5.00, strong slipped two to $4.10 and lamb was down eight at $3.91. The market indicator was down a cent to $4.48.

On offer were 3,011 clean tonnes in 25,513 bales, comprising 45 percent crossbred fleece and 28 percent second shear. Merino fleece, lambswool and second-shear bellies and pieces each made up five percent, four percent was bulky skirtings and two percent halfbred fleece. Fifteen percent was passed in.

Compared with last week's sales, merino fleece 18 and 19 micron was slightly cheaper, and 20 and 23 micron were generally unchanged; merino bulky skirtings were generally unchanged; halfbred fleece 1-2 percent dearer; crossbred fleece 35 micron and finer generally unchanged, and 36 micron and stronger the same to one percent cheaper; second shear the same to slightly cheaper; first lambs 28 micron one percent cheaper and 29 micron generally unchanged; bulky skirtings and second shear bellies and pieces up to 2.5 percent cheaper.
Principal interest came from western Europe, China, Nepal, Turkey and local mills with support from Iran, India and Japan.
